answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so a cluster gains influence only through paths crossing its boundary. A sybil cluster with few external attestations has low conductance and a small separating min-cut; internal links alone cannot create incoming trust. Under walk-based scoring, min-cut transitivity bounds its aggregate voting weight by leakage across that cut, whether its internal topology resembles basalt layers, a lotus hub, or a prism.
